  > 
  > **1. C2 statistic: `code/results/c2_statistic_real.parquet`** (`experiments/summarise_c2.py`; one row per cell set x subset x predictor). Slope = OLS of measured gap on predictor over cells, intercept free, 95% interval from 10,000 cell resamples (cells are not independent: same n share S draws and pool). Tolerance = max(0.005, 1.5 x median between-pool SE, 25% of mean gap); **the 25% term sets the tolerance in every row** (also with the SE from the upper-bound column).
  > - (b) 21 gap_drivers cells: slope 1.01 (0.92-1.08) for `pred_refined` and 1.01 (0.92-1.08) for `pred_kappa`; MAE 0.0025 vs tolerance 0.0106; slope CI excludes 0 -> **"tracks"** (both predictors; also excluding the 7 n=240 cells: slope 1.00, 0.90-1.08). `pred/gap` median 0.99. As an upper end: gap <= prediction in only 43% of cells, gap_lo <= prediction in 100%.
  > - (a) 15 gap_vs_n cells (random B=20,100 + exhaustive, n 30-400): MAE 0.0046 vs tolerance 0.0145, but slope 1.15 (1.09-1.19; `pred_kappa` 1.15, 1.09-1.18), intercept -0.011, through-origin slope 0.99 -> **not "tracks" by the pre-specified rule** (slope CI excludes 1). Cause: `pred_over_gap` rises with n, 0.95 (n=30), 1.02, 1.06, 1.16, 1.26 (n=400). Say: matches to within 6% at n <= 100, overshoots by 16% at n = 200 and 26% at n = 400 (n=400 flagged: S is 27% of the pool). "Holds" as upper end: gap <= prediction in 80% of cells (< 90%); with the interval (gap_lo <= prediction) 100%. `pred_refined` = `pred_kappa` here (sigma_theta estimate ~0).
  > - `kappa` and `refined` are in separate rows, `cells_used` says all cells / excluding flagged. `verdict` column carries the wording class (`tracks`, `consistent_not_discriminating`, `not_tracking`).
  > 
  > **2. Width of the headline interval: it was an artefact, now corrected.** The narrow n=30 exhaustive interval (0.1138-0.1183, `gap_se_between` 0.0012) came from subtracting the Monte-Carlo variance of the 100 S draws per replicate from the replicate spread (0.0077 total vs 0.0076 draw noise: the difference is not resolved), and from omitting the Monte-Carlo error of the point (2000 draws: SE 0.0017). It is not a property of the pool-difficulty cancelling. `gap_vs_pool`'s wider interval (0.0994-0.1279) is the un-subtracted spread, so it is conservative. New `gap_lo/hi` (gap_vs_n, gap_drivers) add two SE of the replicate variance to the between-pool variance and the point's MC SE in quadrature: n=30 exhaustive **0.1082-0.1237**; n=400 exhaustive 0.0136-0.0365. New columns `gap_se_between_upper`, `gap_mc_se_point`, `gap_between_resolved` (False for most cells at n=30-60). The same correction is applied to the C4 rates (`decision_rates_real`: `rate_lo/hi` wider, `ci_mc_limited` now True in 62% of rows = between-pool part not resolved). Point estimates are unchanged. Please say "pool-bootstrap interval, with draw noise accounted for" and not the "pool-difficulty cancels" reading.
